obligations.note: The change makes OutboundClient.url_for rewrite the statement-delivery base URL from https:// to http:// for any path starting with /archive/, so that outbound endpoint no longer uses TLS. The registered 'exhaustive' control test only sends to '/probe', so it never runs the new branch and its pass doesn't establish the obligation.

The INTEGRATIONS list, its names and hostnames, and controls/payments/asset-inventory.json are all unchanged, so every integration stays inventoried with the same host, owner and classification. The exhaustive control test test_integrations_are_inventoried is in the suite and passing.
Ticket CHG-24482 is standard and was approved on 2026-10-12 by grace.kim (change_manager), before the change opened. Its components [payments.integrations] cover the only touched file.
sofia.santos approved a code_review; she is a payments change_approver and a different person from the author, Mara Costa (none of Costa's directory addresses appear).
The code_review and security_review approvals both name head commit aa4e9b6, and that is the change's only commit.

run.json says commit aa4e9b6 passed on ci-runner-08 on 2026-10-14, but the JUnit report is stamped 2026-10-23 from host dev-laptop-7.local, after the 2026-10-16 review time. Its provenance can't be confirmed, and I couldn't re-run the suite here because the available Python is older than 3.11.

payments.integrations is security_sensitive. kofi.mensah (security_reviewer) approved a security_review on head commit aa4e9b6, so the procedural requirement is met, even though the review missed the TLS downgrade.
The only touched file is apps/baseline-payments/payments/integrations.py, which matches none of the protected paths, so no control_owner approval is needed.
The change and ticket are standard, not emergency, so no post-implementation review applies.

The change deviates from ENC-2, but no exception in the register covers ENC-2 or payments.integrations; the register only has SES-1 (expired), LOG-1 (mortgage) and MFA-1 (withdrawn). The deviation has no valid exception.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers apps/baseline-payments/payments/integrations.py, so this change makes no earlier evidence lapse.

summary: The change makes payments send statement-delivery requests to /archive/ paths over plain http by rewriting https:// to http://, which violates ENC-2. CI passes only because the 'exhaustive' TLS control test probes '/probe' and never reaches the new branch. No exception in the register covers this deviation. The ticket, independent code review and security review are procedurally in order, but they approved a TLS downgrade the change description doesn't disclose, and the CI report's provenance is doubtful. The change must be rejected.
